purpose: Visual reference for the independent HTML/SVG instruction-card study
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: visual design study for a browser-based Harmonia product instruction card.
Create a beautifully clear AIRLINE SAFETY CARD style instructional graphic, straight-on, flat on white, landscape 1536 by 1024. This is a software product explanation, NOT an aviation scene. Crisp hand-drawn vector-like navy outlines, flat pale blue fills, small warm orange numbered discs, generous white space. No gradients, no photographic texture, no tiny text, no decorative dashboard UI.
Top left: "Harmonia". Below, the title "One workflow. Independent applications."
Exactly FOUR equally sized panels in a spacious 2 by 2 grid. Each panel has a small orange number at its top left and one short caption, exactly as below. The large drawings tell the story.
Panel 1 number 1, caption "Separate owners": two distinctly different application buildings, a bank and a property office, each with its own owner pictogram and lock. They remain separate.
Panel 2 number 2, caption "Agree a plan": two people at opposite sides of a table point at the same strip of three connected task circles, no merged buildings.
Panel 3 number 3, caption "Keep authority": close-up of an owner's hand stamping a document INSIDE a clearly outlined application boundary; a second hand outside that boundary is stopped by a simple stop mark. Keep the visual gentle and explanatory.
Panel 4 number 4, caption "Resume progress": a laptop closes on the left; a persistent ledger book with a bookmark and two completed task dots stays in the center; a reopened laptop on the right displays the same bookmarked three-dot plan. Do not suggest restarting work.
Bottom: only four tiny connected progress circles, no textual footer, no action buttons, no menus. Use concise captions once only. Preserve roomy margins so figures and arrows never touch labels. This should be possible to recreate with semantic HTML and clean inline SVG. Four distinct handcrafted compositions, unified stroke weight and artistic direction.
